NHC-Catalyzed β-Specific Addition of N-Based Nucleophiles to 
Allenoates
Wenchao Wu, a Shuangli Xu, a Yan Zhang, a Xiu Wang, a Ruotong Li, a Fang Sun, a Chenxia Yu, a 
Tuanjie Li,*a Donghui Wei*b and Changsheng Yao*a
N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) catalyzed regiospecific β-additions of nitrogen-containing nucleophiles including 
nitrogenous heterocycles and trifluoromethylated acylhydrazone to allenoates were accomplished under mild reaction 
conditions, harnessing NHC as a Lewis base to furnish branched N-alkyl compounds in moderate to good yields with high 
E/Z selectivity and broad substrate scope. DFT calculations on the possible reaction mechanisms show that β-addition 
pathway is more energetically favourable than γ-addition pathway, which is in agreement with the experimental 
observations. 
Introduction
Allenes have exhibited high reactivity in comparison to the 
similar alkenes due to their cumulated C-C double bonds, thus 
they have been demonstrated as useful building blocks for the 
construction of complex skeletons.1 After the pioneering work 
of Lu and co-workers,2 allenoates have been proven to undergo 
many types of annulations including [3+2] and [2+n] 
cyclization to establish carbo- or heterocyclic scaffolds.3 In 
particular, the transformations of allenoates under the catalysis 
of nucleophilic amine4 and phosphine5 have received 
considerable interest due to the flexibility of modifying 
molecular complexity.6 In 2008, Marinetti’s group reported a 
phosphine-catalyzed highly enantioselective [3+2] cyclizations 
of ethyl 2,3-butadienoate with α,β-unsaturated esters or ketones 
(Scheme 1a).7 Furthermore, the same reaction promoted by a 
tertiary amine gave pyran derivatives through β,γ-[2+4] 
annulation disclosed by Borhan’s group at a later time (Scheme 
1b).8 So far, N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs) have been 
extensively utilized as nucleophilic catalysts to facilitate the 
conversions of aldehydes,9 acids,10 esters,11 α,β-unsaturated 
aldehydes,12 etc.13 Very recently, the above-mentioned 
reactions catalyzed by NHC performed by our group gave the 
α,β-[2+4] cycloadduct with regioselectivity distinct from the 
annulations facilitated by phosphine or tertiary amine (Scheme 
1c).14 Therefore, we can conclude safely that the structure of 
the products and the reaction selectivity of allenoate-involved 
transformations are mainly reliant on the catalysts.

Recently, the N-alkylation of nitrogen-containing 
heterocycles catalyzed by nucleophilic organic molecular 
catalysts has received enormous attention.15 Many nitrogenous 
heterocycles gracefully exhibit superior biological 
characteristics, such as Losartan,16 Etomidate17 and 
Ruxolitinib.18 And some pyrazole-based Janus kinase (JAK) 
inhibitors were developed successfully (Fig. 1).19 In 2014, Breit 
and coworkers reported the first atom-economic rhodium-
catalyzed regioselective α-umpolung coupling of allenes with 
imidazoles (Scheme 2a).20 Later, a phosphine-catalyzed γ-
addition reaction of allenoates with pyrazole and imidazole 
derivatives through umpolung process was disclosed by 
Virieux’s and Guo’s group (Scheme 2b).21 To continue our 
work on NHC-catalyzed transformations of allenoates and 
study on the dependence of their regioselectivity on catalyst 
further,14,22 we carried out NHC-promoted reactions of 
nitrogenous heterocycles with allenoates, which provided 
regiospecific β-adducts under mild conditions with excellent 
atom economy (Scheme 2c). These results also paved a new

Results and discussion
We commenced our study with the model reaction of 
imidazole (1a) with 2,3-butadienoic acid, ethyl ester (2a), and 
the results were summarized in Table 1. In the presence of 
precatalysts A (20 mol%) and Cs2CO3 (50 mol%), the β-
addition reaction occurred smoothly and provided the 
corresponding product 3aa in 54% yield as a single geometrical 
isomer in THF (Table 1, entry 1). The single crystal X-ray 
diffraction confirmed the structure of 3aa unambiguously (Fig. 
2).23 Other NHC precursors, including imidazolium salts B-D, 
triazolium salts F-H and thiazolium catalyst E, resulted in low 
yield or produced a mixture of E and Z isomers (entry 2-8). 
After a careful screening of the solvents and bases, compound 
3aa was obtained regiospecifically in 58% yield in the presence 
of tBuOK in THF (entry 17). Besides, a blank test was carried

Trifluoromethylated molecules have become a research focus 
in the fields of pesticides and medicines due to their notable 
properties, thus much effort has been devoted to the conversion 
of building blocks with trifuloromethyl group to the new 
chemical entities with specific functions or properties.24 
Meanwhile, N-acylhydrazone (NAH) is a privileged and 
ubiquitous core distributed broadly in hit and lead compounds 
acting on numerous types of molecular targets.25 In 2013, 
Huang’s group reported the first phosphine-catalyzed tunable 
aza-Michael β-addition reaction of allenoates with 
trifluoromethylated acylhydrazones and obtained two 
isomerized products.26 To further expand the substrate scope, 
the trifluoromethylated acylhydrazone was also tested for the 
reaction (Table 3). To our delight, these trifluoromethylated 
substrates were compatible with the reaction conditions and 
provided the single products in good yields with high E/Z 
selectivities as well (Table 3, 5aa-5ga). It should be also 
noteworthy that electron-donating groups on the phenyl ring of 
acylhydrazone such as OMe and Me reduced the product yields 
of 5ca (33%) and 5fa (45%) slightly, respectively.

To get some insight into the reaction pathway and 
chemoselectivity, we have performed DFT calculations by 
using Gaussian16 program, and more computational details can 
be found in Supporting Information. As shown in Figure 4, 
there are two competing reaction pathways associated with the 
structural transformations from R1 and R2 to E/Z-P and P’ 
through two different pathways, respectively. The calculated 
results show that NHC can nucleophilically attack on R1 via 
transition state TSI with an energy barrier of 20.4 kcal/mol to 
form intermediate I, then the different pathways divorced in the 
following steps. One pathway undergoes γ-C protonation by R2 
via transition state TSII, β-C-N bond formation via transition 
state TSIII, dissociation of catalyst and product E-P via 
transition state E-TSIV. It should be noted that the Z-isomer 
pathway associated with E-TSIV and Z-P is obviously 
unfavourable in the energy profile, which is consistent with the 
experimental observation. The other pathway occurs through α-
C protonation by R2 via transition state TS'II, γ-C-N bond 
formation via transition state TS'III, R2-assisted [1,2]-proton 
transfer via transition states TS'IV and TS'V, and dissociation of 
catalyst and product P' via transition state TS'VI. The energy 
barrier of entire reaction associated with E-P is 22.0 kcal/mol, 
which is lower than that associated with P' (26.7 kcal/mol), 
indicating the E-P should be the main product. All the 
calculations are in agreement with the experimental results.

Conclusions
In conclusion, we have described a NHC-catalyzed β-specific 
addition of nitrogen-based pronucleophiles to allenoates, 
offering a new approach towards the heterocyclic and fluorine-
containing substituted Michael olefins with excellent atom 
economy. This protocol represented a new reaction pattern of 
NHC-catalyzed transformations involving allenoates. DFT 
calculations on the possible reaction pathways show that the 
formation of β-adduct is more energetically favourable than 
that of γ-adduct, which is in accordance with the results of the 
experiment. Further studies on the application of this 
methodology are underway in our lab.
